answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post orders, with higher limits earned only after completing audited trades. A cheap fake account then cannot multiply influence for free: every Sybil must tie up capital, and dishonest trades risk slashing that stake. Random audits can sample agents across the market, so hiding a cluster behind names like basalt, island, or comet does not remove the shared financial cost or the chance of detection.
